planting.note: Direct sow or set out divisions after last frost in sandy, saline, or coastal soil; unlike annual Salicornia, perennial glasswort forms a persistent woody base and returns year after year, spreading slowly to form a low mat in salt marsh or brackish garden conditions.

directions: Sow seed or plant divisions in sandy, well-drained, saline to brackish soil in full sun; perennial glasswort is a close relative of annual Salicornia, sharing the same leafless, jointed, succulent green stems and briny, oceanic flavor prized as 'sea beans' or samphire in gourmet cooking, but distinguished by its perennial habit — the base of the plant becomes woody and persists through winter, resprouting fleshy new stems each spring rather than dying back to seed like annual glasswort. This makes it a useful low, spreading edible groundcover for a genuinely saline coastal garden bed, salt marsh restoration planting, or tide-edge landscape where few other edible plants survive, and once established it slowly forms a dense, low mat rather than requiring reseeding each year. Harvest the tender young stem tips through the growing season with scissors, leaving the tougher, woodier base intact to keep producing; flavor and texture are best on actively growing spring and early summer growth before stems begin to harden. Like its annual cousin, it tolerates direct seawater irrigation and thrives in salinity that would kill ordinary vegetables.
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service — GRIN Taxonomy
